newsitem.title: UK: Morgan says has nearly 8.0 pct redemptions.
newsitem.headline: Morgan says has nearly 8.0 pct redemptions.

text.p: Morgan Grenfell said on Thursday it had just under eight percent redemptions in the three previously suspended funds which resumed trading earlier today.
The funds in question are the 444 million stg MG European Capital Growth Fund, the 137 million stg MG Europa Fund and the 788 million stg MG European Growth Trust.

The funds were suspended on Monday due to suspected "irregularities" but resumed trading on Thursday after Morgan Grenfell's parent Deutsche Bank spent 180 million stg removing certain unlisted securities from the funds.

"This is good news because people were predicting they would be selling lots...but there has been no panic selling," said James Murray, a spokesman for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the bank's investment banking arm.
Earlier, Britain's Serious Fraud Office said it was involved in the investigation into the funds.
A spokeswoman said the office was in contact with British investment watchdog IMRO which would share any relevant material with the SFO.
Both fund managers involved with the three funds have been suspended by Morgan Grenfell and the assets of one, Peter Young, have been frozen.
Industry sources said that while Morgan Grenfell would want to put a brave face on the situation, redemptions of eight percent in one day was a major reverse.
"If I had clients who were still in these funds, I'd be advising them to sell straight away," said one money manager who declined to be named. "What would be the point of staying in?"
But asked how the Morgan Grenfell situation was affecting the industry, the money manager said, "Well, on a scale of one to ten, it's about one."
